packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET-09 - unverified image-only reading (working notes appended image by image; summary at end)

== image-001.jpg (reduced overview, first face) ==
A long horizontal parchment strip on a black ground with a wooden ruler below (scale 0-17 cm; the strip is roughly 32 cm long by about 5 cm high, estimated from the ruler). Almost the whole face is BLANK; a vertical fold/crease about 40% along, glue or paste residue (brown) at both short ends and a folded lower edge. Writing survives only as the lower parts of ONE line running along the very top edge, cut through horizontally by the trimming: traces at the left third, a short group just right of the crease, and a longer, darker stretch at the right. One short red oblique stroke stands in that line (right part). No rubric title, initial, running title, column gap or gloss is visible; a single trimmed line cannot show the layout. Faint offset/ghost marks lower right, not legible.

== image-002.jpg (tile, top edge, left third) ==
Single line, upper half of the letters cut away by the edge; brown, faded.
image-002 L1: [.]o(?)/[.]a(?) ... ...ib(us)(?)/...ilz(?) p(ro)...(?)/g...(?) ...) -a(?)/d(?) ...ono(?)/...mo(?) q(ua)n(?)/p(ro)u(?)/t(ame)n(?) ... ...) 
   (only bases and descenders; two long comma-shaped descending strokes, one mid-line and one at the right end, look like the tails of abbreviation signs or of "y"/"h"/-us signs. No word is securely readable.)

== image-003.jpg (tile, top edge, middle; overlaps image-002 at left and image-004 at right) ==
image-003 L1: [overlap: tail stroke) ] [blank stretch across the crease] ...illi(?)/...sili(?) mi(?)...[q/p descender]...is(?)/...m(?) illi(?)/vb(i)(?) ... [faint] ... ill(?)...assu(?)/...asp(er)(?)... [continues in image-004]
   (extremely faint; letters reduced to minims along the cut. Not securely readable.)

== image-004.jpg (tile, top edge, right third; darker ink, the best-preserved stretch; letters appear upright, cut through the upper part) ==
image-004 L1: [overlap: ...assu(?)/...aspu(?)] [red oblique stroke, like a virgule or paraph mark] di(?)/ci(?) or(?)/ut(?) cui(?)/cau(sa)(?) ex(?)/e(st)(?) oi(?)/o(mn)ib(us)(?) / ven(?)/boni(?)... fuit(?)/tan(tum)(?)/sini(?) oi(?)/o(mn)i(u)m(?)/ei(us)(?) rex(?)/tex(tus)(?)/rep(?) i(n)(?) q(ua)tu(m)(?)/q(ua)n(tum)(?)/q(ui)tu(?) [end of line near the right edge; brown paste stain beyond]
   (a small formal book hand, visibly different in style from a cursive - compact, upright; a thin oblique hairline also follows the fifth word. Because the tops are trimmed, c/t, e/c, r/t and u/n/ii cannot be told apart reliably.)

== image-005.jpg (reduced overview, second face of the strip) ==
Same strip, other side, with ruler. Again almost entirely blank (greyish, with remains of paste and modern transparent/paper repair tape along the lower edge and short ends); a vertical fold about 60% along. Writing: (a) ONE line of a small formal book hand along the very top edge, here with the LOWER part trimmed less - upper portions of the letters are present and the bottoms are cut by the edge in places; it survives in three stretches (left, centre, right of the fold) with blank-looking gaps between, which could be abrasion or an intercolumnar/word gap - cannot be decided; (b) below it at the far left, a short note in a different, thinner CURSIVE hand, ending in a long horizontal flourish - an addition under the line (marginal/lower-margin note, tentative); (c) a modern PENCIL inscription in the blank middle: "J. V. IV 28 (5740)" (the roman numeral could also be read "N"/"II"; observed only, not interpreted).
No rubric, initial, running title or underlining visible.

== image-006.jpg (tile, top edge, left part of second face) ==
Main hand (formal), single line:
image-006 L1: [starts a little in from the left edge] ti(?)/tu(m)(?) cu(m)(?)/ei(?)/Q(?)a(?) viueret(?)/bu[..]et(?)/iuuet(?) de(?)/d(icitu)r(?) vbiq(?)/virt(?)/vbi[..](?) [whitish damage, 1-2 letters] ...ius(?)/...tus(?) q(?) no(n)(?)/q(ua)s(?) saluaret(?)/faceret(?)/seruiret(?) [gap] iustificatio(?)/instituatio(?)/iusticiam(?)... [continues in image-007]
   (the second word has a round letter with an abbreviation stroke - "cu(m)", "ei(us)" or a capital "Q"; "viueret" and "saluaret"/"faceret" both show the -eret/-aret ending fairly clearly.)
Added note below, cursive hand, left edge (begins at or beyond the cut left edge):
image-006 L2 (addition): a(?) nob(is)(?)/a nos(?) p(os)t(?)/p(rim)o(?)/p(otes)t(?) exhibent(ur)(?)/exhibeat(ur)(?)/explicit(?) [long horizontal pen flourish to the right]
   (a tall "p" with a superscript letter, then a word beginning with a looped "e"/"c" + "x"/"p" with a long descender. Different ink weight and ductus from L1: an added note, not part of the main line.)

== image-007.jpg (tile, top edge, centre of second face; overlaps image-006 at left and image-008 at right) ==
Only the lower two-thirds of the letters survive (tops cut by the edge).
image-007 L1: [overlap with image-006: iustificatio(?)/instituatio(?)/iustitia(m) d(?)] ip(s)i(?)/ip(s)e(?)/q(ui)a(?) ... [faint, 1-2 words] ...ei(?)/...ra(?) aiaii(?)/anim(?)/vnum(?)/aliam(?) v(er)o(?)/reg(?)/p(ro)p(?) iusti(?)/susti(?)/iussi(?)... [line breaks off; blank to the fold] [fold] [after the fold:] s(?)/f(?)[..]pe(?)/sup(?)... [continues in image-008]
   (one clear descender of "p" with a crossed/looped tail (p(er)/p(ro)) in "ip(s)i"; a "g"/"p(ro)"-like descender before the last word. No word is secure.)

== image-008.jpg (tile, top edge, right part of second face; overlaps image-007 at left) ==
image-008 L1: [overlap: s(?)/f(?)..p(?).. , thin cursive-looking strokes, possibly a different/added hand] ...auit(?)/...tuit(?)/...aiut(?) me(?)/nie(?)/inc(?) h(ic)(?)/n(ec)(?)... . pond(?)/bonu(m)(?)/ponit(?)... [ragged edge, letters lost for about 3-4 cm] ... ...requ(?)/...rcui(us)(?)/...tiqu(us)(?) [-us/-9 sign; end at the right edge]
   (the first group after the fold is in thin strokes with a long "f"/"s" hairline; the rest is the formal hand, with only the lower halves preserved; a mid-line point stands before "pond..". Not securely readable.)

================================================================
PACKET-09 SUMMARY
================================================================
Exposure: nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification of the work or author, or any earlier reading of this strip. I did not attempt to identify the text. Two things visible in the images themselves bear on provenance and I record them only as observations: the modern pencil inscription "J. V. IV 28 (5740)" (image-005) and the ruler. (Separately, in the previous packet a blue "K / UL" stamp was visible; that is a different packet.)
Beyond-the-rules disclosure: none for this packet - only PROMPT.md and image-001..008 were opened; no rotation or other processing; no web, search, catalogue or edition. (I had listed the directory's file names once at the start; packet.json was not opened.)

Layout survey: one long narrow parchment strip (about 32 x 5 cm by the ruler), both faces shown. Each face is blank except for a single line of text running along the top long edge, cut through horizontally when the strip was trimmed - the first face (image-001) keeps only letter-bases, the second face (image-005) keeps most of the letter height on the left and less toward the right. The strip is therefore the lower or upper margin of a leaf (or bifolium - there is a vertical fold on each face) with the edge of the outermost text line; which margin, and how many columns, cannot be told from one line. The main hand is a small upright formal book hand in brown-black ink. One red oblique stroke occurs in the line on the first face (image-004). On the second face a short note in a thinner cursive hand with a long flourish stands under the line at the far left (image-006 L2), and a few thin strokes after the fold (image-008) may be by the same or another adding hand - tentative. No heading, rubric, enlarged initial, running title or underlining is visible. Paste residue, a folded edge and modern repair tape show the strip was reused (binding material - tentative interpretation).

Spans selected: all of the writing there is - image-004 L1 (best stretch on face 1), image-006 L1 and the added note image-006 L2 (best stretch on face 2), and the fainter continuations in image-002, 003, 007, 008. Unread: essentially all of image-002 and image-003 (letter-bases only) and the damaged right half of image-008.

Most usable readings (all still uncertain):
  image-006 L1: "t.. cu(m)(?) viueret(?) de(?) vbi..(?) ...ius q.. no(n)(?) saluaret(?)/faceret(?) [gap] iusti...(?)"
  image-006 L2 (added cursive note): "a nob(is)(?) p..t(?) exhibent(ur)(?)" + flourish
  image-004 L1: "[red stroke] di(?) or(?) cui(?) ex(?) oi(?) / ...(?) fuit(?) oi(?) rex(?)/tex(?) i(n)(?) q(ua)tu(m)(?)"

Limitations: there is no connected text of ten or more lines on either face - one trimmed line per face is all the leaf preserves, so a longer span is impossible, not merely unread. The tiles are low-resolution (letters only a few pixels high) and the line is cut through its height, so c/t/e/r and minim groups are indistinguishable in many places; I have given alternatives rather than chosen. The gaps within the line may be damage or column/word spacing. The relation between the two faces' lines (same text continuing or not) is unknown.
Suggested further views: a much higher-resolution capture of just the top edge of both faces (the present tiles appear to be upscaled from an overview), ideally with the strip flattened so the cut edge lies flat; raking or UV light for the faint left part of face 1 (image-002/003) and the abraded right part of face 2 (image-008); a close-up of the cursive note at image-006 L2.
This is an unverified image reading.
